newsitem.title: UK: UK's Anglian Group sees further progress.
newsitem.headline: UK's Anglian Group sees further progress.

text.p: British home improvements and building products company Anglian Group Plc said on Tuesday that introduction of a specialist sales force in the retail home improvements market would help it continue its progress in the current year that was witnessed in the second half of the previous year.
"Steady progress should continue with demand growth likely to be maintained in the retail and new house build markets," said Eddie Boss, chief executive of Anglian.
The company created a new specialist sales force for each of its major product areas targeted at retail home improvements market and backed it by increased spending on marketing.

The move boosted its retail turnover of Anglian Windows Ltd and Living Design (Home Improvements) Ltd by 19 percent to 177 million stg in the year to March, 1997 from 149.1 million in the previous year.
The company's overall pre-tax profit rose to 20.2 million stg from 16.2 million on a turnover which rose to 223.3 million stg from 194.3 million.
The company's earnings per share rose to 15.5 pence from 12.8 pence and it proposed a final dividend of 5.4 pence a share against 4.5 pence in the previous year.
"Now that the group has been organised for growth in its retail markets, a strong investment in both infrastructure and marketing is taking place," the company said.

The company's operations in the commercial markets was mixed, with local authority replacement window and door sales still remaining difficult, it said. Commercial turnover was slightly ahead at 46.3 million stg against 45.2 million in the previous year.
